studies.prompt: An elderly kindly undead gardener kneels with one boot planted and one knee down, holding a ceramic jug by its handle to water a sapling. Author believable adult proportions, a clear five-digit grip, restrained facial creases and a few stitches without gore. Quiet native cubic contours on charcoal; water is the single bright accent. Use only background-colored occlusion plates, no texture trace, colored fill, gradients or embedded image. Animate a clearly visible five-second returning action: The gardener nods toward the pot and tips the jug with the attached forearm and gripping hand. A changing stream begins during the tip, stops as the jug returns, and the rooted sapling answers with a gentle lean; knee, boot and pot remain fixed. Use authored matching-topology path poses, preserve hand-prop attachment and fixed ground contacts, and keep the action legible at 300 pixels wide.
studies.method: Hand-authored native SVG contours with articulated matching-topology action poses; no raster embedded, automatic paint trace, or whole-frame wobble.

review.notes: Viewed seven native poses at actual 300px size plus full-size anticipation and pouring extremes. Forearm, gripping fingers, jug handle and spout follow a shared tip, while the shoulder, grounded knee, planted boot and pot remain fixed. The stream starts at the moving spout and ends inside the pot; it fades out on the return. The nod and rooted plant response remain secondary. Water is an authored line gesture rather than fluid simulation.
review.limits: Sparse illustrative anatomy; explicit local character action with a fixed camera. Review covers sampled native frames, not continuous playback. SVG-only delivery.

finalMotionReview.reviewer: Main-agent self-review of delegated authoring and subsequent local repairs
finalMotionReview.scope: Static and authored-time pose sheets, full-size peaks where needed, and ten sampled frames from actual automatic browser playback crossing the loop boundary.
finalMotionReview.finding: Arm, gripping fingers and jug tip together; the stream begins at the moving spout and falls inside the pot. Planted boot, knee and pot stay fixed while head and plant give secondary responses.
